memos.headline: S10 and S06 Lead on Trend and Relative Strength; S07 and S05 Show Persistent Weakness
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe as of today. S10 stands out as the strongest name: +5.9% on the week, only -2.3% from its 52-week high, +9.4% above its 50-day mean, and +3.3% relative strength vs SPY over 4 weeks — classic momentum leadership, though RSI at 60.4 and the extended gap above the 50d mean warrant watching for a pullback toward ~210 before adding aggressively. S06 is the steadiest chart here with the lowest ATR (1.60%), just -1.8% off highs, and positive relative strength on both 4w and 12w horizons. On the weak side, S07 is deeply damaged at -23.6% from its 52-week high, trading 6.7% below its 50-day mean with negative 12w relative strength of -11.1% — I would need a reclaim above the 50-day average (~872) to reconsider. S05 is similarly broken, -15.9% off highs, below its 50-day mean, and bleeding relative strength at -11.2% over 12 weeks. I have moderate conviction on the leaders and high conviction on avoiding the laggards.

views.note: Strongest momentum profile in the universe: near 52w highs, +5.9% weekly surge, positive relative strength; would reassess on a close below 210.
Tight, low-volatility uptrend just 1.8% off highs with 12w relative strength of +9.8% vs SPY; risk level is a break below the 50d mean (~350).
Healthy uptrend above both moving averages with moderate RSI of 53.9 and positive relative strength; would turn neutral on a close below 305.
Impressive 12w return of +25.8% but now +12.5% above 50d mean — stretched and vulnerable to mean reversion; wait for a pullback toward ~445 to get long.
Short-term relative strength improving (+4.6% vs SPY 4w) but 12w relative strength flat and 26w return only +3.4% — trend is mediocre; needs to clear 170 for conviction.
Pulling back sharply (-5.8% over 4w) and losing relative strength at -5.4% vs SPY; still above 200d mean so not broken, but needs to hold ~250 or becomes an avoid.
Trading 3.5% below 50d mean with -8.7% 12w relative strength despite strong 26w absolute return — distribution pattern; would reconsider above 410.
Persistent downtrend: -15.9% from highs, below 50d mean, -11.2% 12w relative strength vs SPY — no reason to own until price reclaims 355.
Worst drawdown in the universe at -23.6% from highs, 6.7% below 50d mean, RSI 45.4 and falling — damaged goods until a close above ~870.
Flat-to-down trend: -10.4% over 26w, hugging the 200d mean with -7.9% 12w relative strength — dead money until a breakout above 155.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Lead on Explosive Earnings Growth; S09 and S01 Flash Margin and Growth Warnings
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe. S10 stands out with 106% YoY revenue growth to $96.2B and a 62% net margin, while S05 posted a 93.7% net margin on $119.8B of revenue with net income up nearly 298% YoY—both names exhibit durable, high-quality earnings power with modest debt loads ($33.4B and $14.8B respectively). S04 and S03 also impress: S04 delivered 39.7% net margins and 31.3% net income growth on its 10-K, and S03 grew net income 245% YoY to $62.7B, though its $133B debt stack warrants monitoring. On the other end, S09's 4.9% net margin with a 46% YoY earnings decline and S01's 14.4% margin with a 16% earnings drop signal cash-flow compression I'm unwilling to pay for—any further margin deterioration in either name would confirm the avoid thesis.

views.note: Revenue doubling YoY to $96.2B with a 62% net margin and only $33.4B debt is the best earnings profile in the universe; I'd reassess if margins fall below 50%.
A 93.7% net margin on $119.8B revenue with minimal $14.8B debt and 298% net income growth signals extraordinary earnings power; a margin normalization below 50% would change my view.
Full-year 10-K shows 39.7% net margin, 17.7% revenue growth, and 31.3% net income growth with manageable $40.3B debt—durable compounder.
Net income surged 245% YoY to $62.7B on 19.6% revenue growth, but $133B in total debt tempers conviction; leverage trending higher would flip me neutral.
24% revenue growth and 65% net income growth with a 17.5% margin show improving operating leverage, though $36.2B debt on $20.5B revenue needs watching.
Strong 27.7% revenue growth and 36.9% margin are offset by a massive $460.5B debt load that dominates the balance sheet; need to see deleveraging before getting constructive.
Solid 16.4% revenue growth and 27.2% margin, but $82.3B debt and decelerating growth versus peers keep me on the sideline; margin expansion above 30% would turn me long.
Revenue essentially flat at +0.4% YoY with a thin 4.9% margin; the 61% net income bounce is off a depressed base and $73.3B debt is heavy relative to earnings.
Net income fell 46% YoY to $4.2B on anemic 2.4% revenue growth with a 4.9% margin—classic cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for.
Full-year 10-K shows revenue up only 1.5% with net income declining 15.8% and $29.3B debt on $21.2B revenue; earnings power is eroding.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause but Sticky 3.3% CPI and Rising Long Yields Argue Against Duration and Favor Banks and Energy
memos.body: I see a regime that has shifted from easing to an extended pause: the upper bound has sat at 3.75% for three months after 75bp of cuts over the prior year, yet headline CPI is running at 3.3% YoY—well above target—while unemployment has actually ticked down 20bp over both 3- and 12-month horizons to 4.10%. The 10y yield at 4.78% is up 61bp over the past year and 31bp over just three months, steepening the curve modestly (10y-2y at +43bp) but punishing duration assets. This combination of resilient labor, above-target inflation, and rising term premia favors short-duration value sectors—banks benefit from a positively sloped curve and stable front end, energy and cyclicals benefit from nominal growth, while long-duration growth equities and rate-sensitive staples face headwinds. A CPI print dropping below 2.8% or unemployment rising above 4.4% would flip my regime call back toward easing and duration-friendly positioning.

views.note: Banks benefit from a positively sloped yield curve (+43bp 10y-2y) and a stable fed funds rate supporting net interest margins.
Energy names thrive in a nominal-growth environment with sticky 3.3% inflation and a tight labor market keeping demand firm.
Cyclicals should hold up given unemployment falling to 4.10% and no imminent recession signal from the now-positive curve.
Duration-sensitive growth faces a headwind from the 10y yield surging 61bp YoY to 4.78%, compressing multiples.
Staples' bond-proxy appeal diminishes as the 10y yield rises sharply and the Fed shows no urgency to cut further.
Broad market is caught between resilient employment and rising discount rates; I lack conviction on direction here.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence Favors S03, S04, S10; Warns on S08, S05
memos.body: I see a clear split in post-earnings sentiment across the universe this cycle. S03 (+15.3%), S04 (+15.5%), and S10 (+8.7%) all printed strong positive price reactions on their results filings, suggesting narrative momentum that may still have room to run—especially S10, whose earnings print is the most recent (Aug 26) and was followed by a new material agreement and an Other Events 8-K on Sep 3, signaling ongoing corporate activity. On the negative side, S08 (-7.4% on earnings, plus a director departure/appointment amendment on Sep 1) and S05 (-7.1% on earnings with only a generic Other Events filing since) look like deteriorating narratives where tone has not yet turned. S07 (+5.6%) and S06 (+2.5%) had mildly positive reactions but lack the magnitude to signal a durable shift; I treat those as neutral. S01's modest -1.9% decline on Q4 results, combined with multiple Reg FD and officer-change filings, reads as noisy rather than directional.

views.note: Massive +15.3% earnings-day pop signals a genuine positive narrative shift that likely has further to run.
+15.5% earnings reaction plus a fresh Reg FD disclosure on Sep 2 suggest sustained positive sentiment momentum.
Recent +8.7% earnings pop, a new material agreement, and an Other Events filing yesterday point to an improving narrative still being digested.
-7.4% earnings selloff followed by a director change amendment suggests negative tone has not stabilized.
-7.1% earnings reaction with no subsequent positive catalyst; tone remains negative with no sign of inflection.
+5.6% earnings reaction was decent but not outsized; new debt agreement on Sep 1 adds uncertainty.
Mild +2.5% earnings reaction and routine corporate filings suggest sentiment is flat—no strong signal either way.
Small -1.9% Q4 reaction amid multiple Reg FD and officer-change filings reads as noise rather than a directional shift.
Tepid +1.2% earnings reaction with no follow-up filings leaves sentiment ambiguous.

memos.headline: Oil Spike and Rising Policy Uncertainty Signal Geopolitical Stress Despite Calm Credit Markets
memos.body: I see a divergence worth flagging: WTI crude surged 12.9% over the past month to $92.55/bbl while the Economic Policy Uncertainty index jumped 31.9% m/m to 245.61, yet VIX at 14.32 and HY OAS at 2.65% remain benign and declining. This pattern—energy stress plus policy uncertainty without broad risk-off—typically reflects a geopolitical supply disruption or sanctions escalation that credit markets have not yet priced. Without specific GDELT event detail in the evidence, I cannot pinpoint the catalyst, but the oil move is large enough to matter for energy-exposed and energy-consuming names across the universe. A reversal in crude below $85 or a drop in the EPU index below 200 would change my view; conversely, if HY OAS begins widening toward 3.0% I would become more defensive across the board. I have moderate conviction on energy beneficiaries and caution on names with high input-cost or geopolitical-supply-chain exposure.

views.note: Two 8-K filings in rapid succession (Aug 17 and Sep 3) suggest active corporate developments, but without content detail I cannot determine geopolitical exposure; staying neutral pending clarity.
Fresh Reg FD filing on Sep 2 may relate to guidance amid the oil spike, but absent disclosure content I lack conviction on direction.

Three Reg FD filings in two weeks in late July hint at material developments; combined with the 32% surge in policy uncertainty, I worry about geopolitical or regulatory headwinds until more detail emerges.
July filings (Reg FD and 8.01) predate the oil spike; no recent updates reduce my ability to assess current geopolitical positioning.
Single 8.01 filing in August provides minimal signal; benign credit spreads suggest no immediate distress but the EPU jump warrants monitoring.
If S07 has energy-sector exposure, the 13% crude rally is a tailwind; Reg FD filing in early August may have previewed favorable positioning, though I need sector confirmation to raise confidence.
